body:
DESMONTANDO OPERETAS
A los periodistas que están tan ardidos por mi contrargumento a la frase de "la gente no llega a fin de mes; se quedan sin plata al día 20" entiendo que se sientan mal por haber repetido como loros una frase sin sentido.

Ahora bien, en lugar de caer en todo tipo de falacias como la "ad populum" (por ej. "todos los encuestadores dicen" o la "ad hominem" (contesta en forma burlona, le falta calle) propongo que demuestren no ser tan precarios y contesten "¿cómo vive durante 10 días una persona sin comer y sin beber?

Si van a usar el argumento del uso de la tarjeta, más allá que demuestra que no son dignos de crédito por ignorantes, sugiero que se pregunten ¿qué ocurre al mes siguiente? Y así repetir el ejercicio hasta que entiendan la lógica intertemporal del crédito. 

Por otra parte, el argumento contra la opereta de la mora fue refutado varias veces. Esto es, si no lo entienden sugiero escucharlo todas las veces que sea necesario hasta que entiendan así no repiten estupideces. Esto es, traten de entender cómo ha cambiado el crédito, los préstamos de altas tasas y bajo monto y la dinámica después de un shock político con freno en el crédito. Entiendo que en general son muy pobres intelectualmente pero no es tan difícil. 

CIAO!

body:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Reconfigure my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), audit (checks the diff).
3. Set isolation: worktree on audit so its checks never touch my working branch.
4. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: delegate every repo search and test run to the Haiku 5.5 subagents to keep the main context small.
5. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

According to Korean media, Elon Musk's Terafab is now talking to almost EVERY Korean chip supplier it can find.

Until now, the only known Korean suppliers were HPSP and Hanmi Semiconductor.

Now TheElec reports that Tesla and SpaceX are in talks across nearly every category Korean companies can supply, from basic piping parts to process materials to test components.

At SEMICON West in San Francisco last week, Terafab staff walked straight to around 10 Korean booths on the morning of day one, including ENF Technology, Dongjin Semichem, Hanmi Semiconductor, Unisem and MiCo.

Several companies have already signed NDAs. One got an NDA by email the same evening Terafab visited its booth.

Hanmi Semiconductor is discussing TC bonders for Terafab, and HPSP has agreed to supply one high pressure hydrogen annealing tool to the R&D line.

MiCo's cleaning unit Komico signed a three way NDA with Tesla and SpaceX about a month ago, and ISC is already swapping samples for rubber test sockets.

Tesla and SpaceX do not buy from Chinese suppliers. One Korean supplier put it simply, without China there are only a few options, and Japan is expensive.

They also want prices that are CHEAPER than China.

$LRCX and $AMAT have reportedly built dedicated Terafab teams, and Fujifilm is meeting Terafab buyers regularly on slurries, photoresist and etchants.

The goal is a fab with 1 million wafer starts per month within 10 years, with $16.8 billion of initial investment and more than 3,000 jobs.

SpaceX broke ground in Grimes County, Texas this month, and the first 100,000 wafer per month phase is expected before 2030.

Logic is being done with $INTC, talks with $TSM are ongoing, and memory will be built separately.

One supplier said that if they email Terafab in the middle of the night in the United States, they get an answer in 30 minutes to an hour.

$TSLA and $SPCX are building a chip supply chain at Elon speed.

Илон Маск предлагает не охлаждать чипы для космоса, а наоборот — пусть работают горячими.

Вот в чём настоящий парадокс космических дата-центров.

Все думают: «В космосе же −270 °C, чипы будут охлаждаться сами». На деле всё наоборот. В вакууме нет ни воздуха, ни воды, которые могли бы уносить тепло. Вакуум работает как огромный термос: тепло, которое выработал чип, остаётся внутри. Единственный способ от него избавиться — излучать его в виде инфракрасного света с больших радиаторных панелей.

И тут начинается жёсткая физика. Чем холоднее радиатор, тем слабее он излучает. По закону Стефана–Больцмана мощность излучения растёт пропорционально **четвёртой степени** абсолютной температуры. Если поднять рабочую температуру чипа всего на 20 % в кельвинах, радиаторы начинают излучать в два раза больше тепла. Значит, их можно сделать в два раза меньше и легче.

Именно об этом говорит Маск в видео:  
«Если увеличить рабочую температуру на 20 % в кельвинах, массу радиаторов можно сократить вдвое. Поэтому в космосе выгодно работать на более высокой температуре».

На Земле мы тратим миллиарды, чтобы держать чипы холодными. В космосе выгоднее спроектировать чипы так, чтобы они спокойно работали при 100–120 °C. Тогда радиаторы становятся существенно легче, а стоимость запуска резко падает. Плюс нейросети довольно устойчивы к случайным битовым ошибкам от радиации — для огромной модели несколько перевёрнутых битов почти ничего не значат.

Получается, что главная проблема космического ИИ — не энергия (солнце в космосе бесплатное и постоянное), а именно теплоотвод. И Маск предлагает решать его не охлаждением, а температурой.

Выглядит почти контринтуитивно, но физика на его стороне.

quote_body:
Former $GOOGL employee on why data center capacity and electricity are the real bottlenecks, not GPU production itself, and how unreliable some of the neoclouds are ($AMZN, $GOOGL, $MSFT, $NVDA):

1. According to the expert, open-source models are closing the gap with frontier models faster than expected, with customers increasingly replacing Anthropic and OpenAI models in multi-agent architectures with open-source alternatives starting from Q2 of this year. The shift started with simple tasks like tool calling and MCP, but has moved up the stack to low-level orchestration.

2. The expert identifies capacity as the biggest constraint at the moment, with certain companies' traffic growing 5x while GPU availability, particularly in the U.S. where latency requirements are tightest, simply cannot keep up. Sourcing capacity overseas in Asia or Australia is technically possible but adds latency that most customers will not accept.

3. Hyperscalers offer reliability but are expensive, require multi-year commitments of three or more years, and have limited availability of the latest hardware, with customers already chasing B300s. AI-native companies tend to gravitate toward neoclouds due to hyperscaler pricing and contract rigidity, but neoclouds come with their own reliability issues, with GPUs dropping off unexpectedly and requiring engineering resources to manage fleet stability around the clock.

4. The third tier consists of smaller independent operators who have invested in GPU racks, seeing the opportunity to lease out capacity and recoup costs within a year or two, with the remainder being pure profit. The expert describes these as essentially unusable in practice, with operators who do nothing more than find land, install racks, connect electricity, and set up cooling, with no real cloud management, maintenance, or operational expertise behind them.

5. The expert expects overall GPU availability to increase meaningfully over the next year or two, with $NVDA continuing to ramp production. The real bottleneck is not GPUs themselves but data center capacity and electricity in the U.S. On the supply side, the expert also sees players $SPCX beginning to lease out spare capacity to the market, with more likely to follow.

6. The expert notes that U.S.-based neoclouds typically require 20-30% prepayment upfront, with the remainder paid monthly or quarterly over the contract term, and rebates negotiated at the end for any reliability incidents like traffic loss. APAC-based providers operate differently, with no prepayment required at all.

EL TESLA ROADSTER PODRÁ VOLAR, PERO NECESITARÁ 7 HORAS DE RECARGA

Lectura rápida
Tesla presentó en Texas una demostración de su nuevo Roadster, un deportivo eléctrico que promete acelerar de 0 a 96 km/h en menos de un segundo, circular boca abajo y realizar saltos sobre otros vehículos. El modelo combina motores eléctricos de hasta 1.360 CV con propulsores de aire comprimido desarrollados junto a SpaceX. Su llegada al mercado está prevista para 2028.

Cómo funciona
El vehículo utiliza ventiladores bajo el piso para aumentar la adherencia y propulsores que expulsan aire comprimido para generar empuje adicional. Su tecnología incluye componentes derivados de los cohetes de SpaceX y motores del robot humanoide Optimus. La versión Rocket incorpora 10 propulsores direccionales que permiten elevar el auto, controlar sus movimientos en el aire y amortiguar los aterrizajes.

La limitación de 7 horas
El tanque de 200 litros de la versión Thrust se vacía en apenas seis segundos de funcionamiento a máxima potencia. La versión Rocket dispone de 600 litros de aire comprimido, cuya recarga mediante el compresor integrado demora entre seis y siete horas. Tesla trabaja para reducir ese tiempo a 30 minutos antes del lanzamiento comercial previsto para 2028.

Versiones
La gama incluirá una versión básica de 1.088 CV, con una autonomía estimada de entre 483 y 515 kilómetros; la Thrust, capaz de acelerar de 0 a 96 km/h en 0,8 segundos; y la Rocket, monoplaza, que promete hacerlo en 0,55 segundos y estará reservada a clientes seleccionados.

quote_body:
Quién ganó el debate entre Lula y Bolsonaro y la insólita estrategia que se hizo viral
 
Gestos calculados, insultos, acusaciones de corrupción y referencias a Donald Trump y Javier Milei marcaron el primer debate televisivo entre Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva y Flavio Bolsonaro, una semana antes del balotaje presidencial en Brasil. Pero detrás de los cruces entre el presidente izquierdista y el senador ultraderechista, una de las principales estrategias de la noche estuvo fuera de los discursos: convertir cada reacción, mueca y provocación en un video viral para las redes sociales.
 
Flavio Bolsonaro, de 45 años, había ensayado durante toda la semana con su estratega de marketing, Duda Lima, y otros integrantes de su equipo una táctica destinada a generar imágenes de confrontación con Lula, de 80 años. La idea era ubicarse detrás del mandatario mientras hablaba a cámara, hacer gestos de desaprobación y mantener una expresión impasible para producir escenas que después pudieran editarse y circular en las plataformas digitales.
 
En ese sentido, la estrategia tuvo éxito: después del debate, se multiplicaron los memes del senador “persiguiendo” a su rival durante el duelo e incluso las imágenes generadas con inteligencia artificial que mostraban a distintos personajes parados detrás de Lula.

body:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Reconfigure my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), audit (checks the diff).
3. Set isolation: worktree on audit so its checks never touch my working branch.
4. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: delegate every repo search and test run to the Haiku 5.5 subagents to keep the main context small.
5. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."
